public_note: This package was found in the Noether Multilingual lane and sense-checked locally after the latest published Noether Zenodo version. It is a multilingual translation handoff/checkpoint for Ukrainian, Russian, Interslavic Latin, and Interslavic Cyrillic, not an independent source-critical or certified critical edition layer.

files.quality_label: Noether Slavic multilingual translation handoff: Ukrainian, Russian, Interslavic Latin, and Interslavic Cyrillic through Papers 01-21; Paper 22 intro is WIP only
files.coverage: The archive README/status files report completed rendered/audited cumulative translation checkpoints through Noether Papers 01-21 in four Slavic branches. ZIP integrity test passes. Cumulative PDFs are present for Ukrainian, Russian, Interslavic Latin, and Interslavic Cyrillic. Paper 21 checkpoint logs report source/structure, text/log, raster-margin, visual-inspection, merge-manifest, and final-sanity checks, and the Paper 21 sanity/audit JSON files report validation pass. Local spot rendering of first/middle/last cumulative pages found nonblank A4 pages with Cyrillic/math rendering intact. A local placeholder/mojibake grep over visible translation TeX found no `????`, replacement-character, TODO/FIXME, placeholder, missing, or omission markers in the completed Papers 01-21 TeX layer.
files.limitations: This is an all-in-one handoff bundle, not a clean reader-only release. It includes provenance/log/source-update material and a bundled 7-Zip tool subtree with executable binaries. It deliberately excludes bulky source-scan PDFs and therefore depends on the existing Noether source records and source-witness packages. Paper 22 is explicitly not complete, and the Paper 22 working terminology seed/log contains real question-mark mojibake in Ukrainian/Russian term entries, so Paper 22 should be reseeded before promotion or continuation. A recheck also found real question-mark mojibake in some completed-branch sidecar terminology/glossary JSON/log material, especially around Paper 09 and Paper 17, so those support glossaries should not be treated as authoritative terminology data until repaired even though the visible reader TeX did not show the same placeholder markers. The Slavic branches were built against their recorded Noether source/control state; newer local German source-audit findings and fixes still require synchronization/propagation before these branches can be called current against the latest local audit state.
files.next_action: Either upload this ZIP as a clearly labelled Noether multilingual handoff/provenance package in the next Noether Zenodo version, or first derive a cleaner public reader/source package that excludes bundled executables and old source-update baggage. In either case, do not describe it as a critical edition or source-closed Noether corpus.
